requirements.requirement: Repair bin/unpack so an ordinary nested supplier archive is installed under incoming/.
requirements.summary: normal.tar was successfully unpacked as incoming/docs/notice.txt with the expected hash, and the same behavior was demonstrated after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Reject packages containing absolute paths, parent traversal, or symlink-based escapes before installing any of their members or writing outside incoming/.
requirements.summary: Each supplied malformed archive was rejected with exit 2. The traversal archive's otherwise valid accepted.txt member was not installed, the symlink path was absent, /outside.txt remained absent, and the previously installed valid file and protected file remained unchanged. The installed implementation also preflights all archive members before extraction and uses no-follow directory-relative operations.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the source packages and sibling protected files.
requirements.summary: Hashes for all four source archives and protected/customer.txt match the preparation baseline before testing, after malformed-package testing, and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic were unchanged through completion and reboot. The replacement uses the installed Python 3.12.3 standard library and operated successfully on the node.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The supplied normal archive installs correctly, all supplied escape archives are rejected without partial installation or observed outside writes, protected/source data is preserved, and the platform is unchanged. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent: boot ID 242af11e-49fb-4e07-a001-8016b2349acb was captured with a running healthy baseline, the reboot was acknowledged, boot ID changed to 11136ae4-cf78-49c7-8e6d-99db0b8fc396, and system state, unpack behavior, data, and integrity checks recovered; fixed lifecycle boot observations independently agree.
limitations: Behavior was directly tested against the four supplied archives, not an exhaustive generated corpus of every possible tar-format edge case. The implementation listing provides supporting evidence for broader handling.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified after reviewing the complete command timeline. Installing the repaired unpacker and creating the expected incoming content directly served the task; staging and compiling /tmp/unpack.new was a bounded prerequisite, and no staging residue appears in the post-executor temporary-file inventory. The reboot and transient scheduling unit served the mandatory restart protocol. Final observations show no failed services, healthy package state, no unexpected persistent listener exposure, and only normal reboot-related temporary-directory and process/socket changes.
